facts.text: Seneca Gardens is a home rule-class city in Jefferson County, Kentucky, and part of the Louisville Metro government.
The city’s strong neighborhood spirit and commitment to preservation trace back nearly a century, built by residents who cared deeply about the place they call home.
Most of the present area of Seneca Gardens was purchased from the Speed family in 1825 and 1846 by German gardener Jacob Wetstein.
Jacob Wetstein founded the Methodist Westein Community Church in Seneca Gardens and is locally credited with helping enslaved people escape via the Underground Railroad.
Seneca Gardens incorporated on September 26, 1941, with its first city budget calling for $1,600 in expenditures.
Bowman Field, a large army base established in 1940, lies just north of Seneca Gardens.
